clue.text: Cry when the batting side makes exactly 100

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

parts.words: when the batting side makes exactly
parts.note: a cricket team is all out when its innings ends with every batsman dismissed, the total it has made then being final

explanation.surface: A cricket fan shouts as the team's score reaches a round hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is 'all out' when its innings closes; all out for exactly 100 is written C ALL OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To call out is to shout or yell aloud a cry.

clue.text: Succeed, but not as a buck-jumper

definitions.meaning: to work out well, as a plan does
a bucking horse makes its rider fall from the saddle, the other sense of the phrase, which the clue says is not meant

explanation.surface: A rodeo rider triumphs by staying on rather than being thrown.
explanation.walkthrough: A buck-jumper is a horse that bucks; the clue warns against the 'fall off the horse' sense of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that comes off works out, so the phrase means to prove a success.

clue.text: In a nursery game they appear on board with 50 snakes

definitions.text: In a nursery game they appear on board

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
adders are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: Describing the board of a children's game where pieces rise and fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Snakes and Ladders is a children's board game; the snakes in the clue are the wordplay, not the game's.
explanation.definitionFit: The rungs climbed up the board in Snakes and Ladders are the game's other feature beside the snakes.

clue.text: Start where actors meet?

definitions.meaning: the beginning of something
actors gather on the set of a film or play, read as two words

explanation.surface: Asking where performers first come together.
explanation.definitionFit: The beginning of an illness or season is its first stage or commencement.

clue.text: Experimenting with holding open court

definitions.meaning: testing something to see how it works
a judge trying a case out in public is hearing it in open court

explanation.surface: A judge who tests new methods while sitting in public session.
explanation.definitionFit: Testing a thing out is putting it to trial, experimenting with it.

clue.text: As far as you can hear someone must be talking about you

definitions.text: As far as you can hear
definitions.meaning: the range within which sound carries

definitions.text: someone must be talking about you
definitions.meaning: folklore says your ears grow hot or burn when you are being discussed

explanation.surface: Within hearing range, someone is gossiping about you.
explanation.definitionFit: Within hearing range is within the reach of the ears, the sound distance.

clue.text: Woodcutter upset over writing tests

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word for the woodcutter upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: an axe is a tool that cuts wood
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A lumberjack is distressed by written assessments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woodcutter' suggests a lumberjack, but it is the tool; 'upset' turns it upside down in this down entry, and 'over' places it above the writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal written assessments at school or college are tests.

clue.text: Legendary outlaw tells how to commit masked burglary

definitions.meaning: the hero of Sherwood Forest in English folklore

definitions.text: tells how to commit masked burglary
definitions.meaning: read as three words, it says steal while wearing a hood

explanation.surface: A famous bandit gives instructions for robbing in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk hero who robbed the rich in Sherwood is the archetypal legendary bandit.

clue.text: A dogged policeman

parts.note: dogged seems to mean persistent, but here it means accompanied by a dog, as a police officer working with one is

explanation.surface: A persistent officer who never gives up.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer who trains and works with a police dog has that title.

clue.text: He needs many coaches for Electrical Engineering

definitions.note: a pronoun standing for the person being taught

parts.note: a railway train is a string of coaches
EE is the abbreviation for electrical engineering

explanation.surface: A student of electrical engineering needs plenty of tutors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coaches' suggests tutors, which suits the definition, but here they are railway carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner being taught a job is a person under instruction, as the pronoun stands for.

clue.text: A way with a pen to demonstrate humility

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A writer uses a pen in a way that shows humility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' suggests writing, but it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Humility is lack of vanity, the quality of being unassuming.

clue.text: Against communism it has introduced a boycott inter alia

indicators.note: the Latin word inter means between or among, so the boycott is set among the letters

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition, a boycott

explanation.surface: A nation opposed to communism has imposed a boycott, among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' stands for the country; 'Against communism' places it in its post-communist era. 'inter' (Latin, among) puts BAN inside ALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun stands for the Balkan country, a nation once ruled by a communist regime.

clue.text: One's attached to manifest nuances

indicators.note: one piece is joined on to the end of the other, which is the order the answer takes

parts.note: overt means open, manifest
read as ones, the plural of one

explanation.surface: A person bound to obvious subtleties.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtle implications or undertones are nuances of meaning.

clue.text: It is used in many long tights

definitions.text: It is used in many long tights

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the two words many long, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A material commonly used in long hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: The synthetic fibre is the classic material of stockings and tights.

clue.text: Joined American investment in that country's central bank

indicators.note: investment in suggests putting money in, but here one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: the Fed is the Federal Reserve, the central bank of the United States
US is short for United States, American

explanation.surface: An American puts money into the Federal Reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Things joined are united or melted together into one.

clue.text: Go off by oneself to sketch detail

parts.note: to sketch is to draw
a detail is a part of something

explanation.surface: Withdraw alone to do some drawing of fine points.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw or separate from others is to go off alone.

clue.text: Going astray during college vacation

definitions.meaning: wandering from the right route
when no course of study is running at college

explanation.surface: A student wanders off during the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship deviating from its route is astray, wandering wrongly.

clue.text: Lesson One taken by a new toddler

definitions.meaning: the opening stage of learning
a toddler's first pace when learning to walk

explanation.surface: A small child's initial lesson in walking.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening move in any undertaking is its beginning, like a baby's first pace.

clue.text: Glance behind, and take care

definitions.meaning: to gaze following someone departing
to tend or mind someone

explanation.surface: Peering over one's shoulder and being careful.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend or watch over someone is to mind them, and to gaze following them is the literal sense.

clue.text: Final dust up for those who like to take a back seat

definitions.text: for those who like to take a back seat
definitions.note: describes the seats at the very rear, where the shy sit

parts.note: last means final
a dust-up is a quarrel or row

explanation.surface: A final squabble among people who prefer to stay in the background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take a back seat' means avoid attention, but here literally the seats at the very rear.
explanation.definitionFit: The rearmost line of seats is where people who shun attention sit.

clue.text: Theoretically working as a journalist

definitions.meaning: in theory rather than practice
employed on a newspaper

explanation.surface: In theory, someone is a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true in theory but untested holds as written down, in principle only.

clue.text: Draw up a banker's cheque

definitions.meaning: to write a first version of a document
an order for payment drawn by a bank

explanation.surface: Preparing a cheque issued by a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw up a document is to prepare a rough version, and a bank's payment order is the second sense.

clue.text: Sesame was his open secret when making a one pound rum cake

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra
I is the Roman numeral for one
a baba is a small sponge cake soaked in rum syrup

explanation.surface: A baker making a rum cake keeps a recipe secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open Sesame' was the password to the thieves' cave in the Arabian Nights tale; 'open secret' plays on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodcutter of the Arabian Nights opened the robbers' cave with the password Open Sesame.

clue.text: Judge which feature most distinguishes a pelican

definitions.meaning: old British slang for a magistrate

definitions.text: which feature most distinguishes a pelican
definitions.meaning: a pelican is known for its huge pouched bill

explanation.surface: Deciding what makes a pelican stand out.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a magistrate is 'the beak'.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate was nicknamed for the nose, and a pelican's bill is its most striking feature.

clue.text: The day after Aug 31 a tint of autumn appears

parts.note: 1 September, written Sep 1, with the figure as the letter I

explanation.surface: On the first of September a hint of autumn colour shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownish photographic shade is a reddish-brown tint.

clue.text: Be just in time to prepare a potato for crisps

definitions.meaning: to leave very little margin
slicing a potato thinly for crisps (chips in American English)

explanation.surface: Hurrying to slice potatoes for snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving barely enough time is to slice the margin thin, like potato slices.

clue.text: Statement of belief by film director ofThe Third Man

definitions.meaning: a set of principles of faith
Carol Reed directed the 1949 film, written as initial and surname

explanation.surface: A manifesto from the director of a classic film noir.
explanation.definitionFit: A confession of faith is a formal statement of belief, and C. Reed is the director's name.

clue.text: Try a letter of query when feeling irritable

parts.note: to test is to try
the letter Y is pronounced like why, a query word

explanation.surface: Someone tries writing an enquiry letter when cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy means irritable or easily annoyed.

clue.text: Substitute heavy fabric with very fine fabric

parts.note: rep is a heavy ribbed fabric
lace is a delicate openwork fabric

explanation.surface: A dressmaker swaps heavy cloth for delicate material.
explanation.definitionFit: To substitute is to put one thing in another's place.

clue.text: Time property is covered by a will

parts.note: an estate is property

explanation.surface: Eventually property passes under a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dies having left a legal will is said to have died so.

clue.text: Serge is beaten

definitions.meaning: a twilled woollen cloth, made from yarn of that kind
defeated

explanation.surface: A man called Serge has lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a woollen cloth of smooth spun yarn, and to be bested is to be beaten.

clue.text: Back pay transposed to settle a debt

indicators.note: the two words are swapped round, so their letters come in a new order

explanation.surface: Arrears of wages are swapped round to clear what is owed.
explanation.definitionFit: To repay is to return money owed, settling a debt.
